Because the meaning of abrogation is the nullification of that text, and nullifying a text is serious. Therefore a person must refrain from declaring abrogation regarding what has not been established as abrogated. Moreover, people's abandoning acting upon something does not indicate that it is actually abrogated, for how many definitive rulings have people abandoned acting upon? People's abandonment of acting upon it is either out of laxity, or because the cause requiring seeking permission has ceased.

The fifteenth benefit: in the verse also is the affirmation of knowledge and wisdom for God from these two names: ﴿And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise⁠﴾. We have previously said that wisdom (ḥikma) means placing things in their proper places. Indeed, we have also previously said that al-Ḥakīm does not mean merely one who possesses wisdom, but one who possesses judgment (ḥukm) and wisdom.

**Student:** (...) O Shaykh, the rule is that hardship brings ease.

**The Shaykh:** Yes. In it, hardship brings ease. Let us look at the author's words, because he has a comment on this verse.

* * *

He said: (The verse about seeking permission: it was said to be abrogated, and it was said: no, but people were lax in abandoning seeking permission.)

These are the two views we pointed to. The correct view is that the verse is definitive and remains in force, and that abandoning seeking permission is either due to laxity or due to the cause requiring permission having ceased. As for saying that legal rulings are abrogated by people abandoning acting upon them, this has no basis.

**Student:** Shaykh, some people say: in abandoning...

**The Shaykh:** In abandoning seeking permission.

**Student:** He did not say: "laxity regarding seeking permission."

**The Shaykh:** No, in its abandonment: "people were lax in abandoning it," meaning: so they abandoned it. You intend that the one who should say, regarding its performance, "they were lax with it," is not said regarding its performance but regarding its abandonment. It is also suitable to say "people were lax": with what were they lax, or what was the cause of their laxity? It is: abandoning seeking permission.

**Student:** (...)

**The Shaykh:** Yes. From disobedience. This is a violation. If he was negligent, we restricted it: if he was negligent in raising and disciplining him. But if he was not negligent, then no.

**Student:** If he is an adult?

**The Shaykh:** No. If he is an adult, then he has become independent in himself. But if he reaches adulthood, he becomes like others: if he is able to change the evil he committed, it is obligatory upon him.

We also discussed yesterday the matter of His saying: ﴿There is no blame on you or on them after these⁠﴾. We said: the verse has an explicit meaning (manṭūq) and an implied meaning (mafhūm). Its explicit meaning is not problematic, which is the negation of blame, because (...) blame.

But its implied meaning is that there is blame on them during these three times, on the guardians and on the children. This is problematic, because children are not legally responsible, so that blame could fall on them for disobedience.

**Student:** We said: the implied meaning (...), and the explicit meaning is true by one of the individual cases.

**The Shaykh:** Yes. We say: the implied meaning has no generality, so it is true by the existence of one instance of the generality, even if just one instance.

* * *

Then he said: (﴿And when the children among you reach puberty⁠﴾, O free ones, ﴿let them seek permission⁠﴾ at all times ﴿as those before them sought permission⁠﴾, i.e., the free adults.)

When they reach puberty, the author says: (﴿among you⁠﴾, O free ones). This is because slaves, as previously mentioned, only seek permission at the three times, whether they are adults or children. Therefore the author restricted it to free people, based on the implied meaning of the first verse.

His saying "reached puberty" (balaghū al-ḥulm) is a metaphor for reaching puberty by emission (al-inzāl). And ḥulm means either dreaming (al-iḥtilām) or intellect, because of the perfection of their intellect. But the first is better, because perfection of intellect is not a requirement here, and perfection of intellect is attained at the completion of forty years.

His saying, "when they reach puberty": ﴿let them seek permission⁠﴾. God, may He be exalted, mentioned only reaching puberty.

It is well known that there are two other things by which puberty is attained: completing fifteen years, and the growth of pubic hair (inbāt shaʿr al-ʿāna). But these two matters are subject to disagreement among scholars.

Some hold that there is no puberty except by emission, and that completing fifteen years is not a sign of puberty, but a sign of a person's ability to fight in jihad, because those who adopted it relied only on the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: «When he was presented to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Uhud, he did not permit him, and when he was presented to him on the day of the Trench, he permitted him» (ﷺ).[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2664) and Muslim (1868/91), from Ibn ʿUmar.]] He was fifteen years old on the day of the Trench. But in a narration of al-Hakim he said: «He did not permit me, and he did not see me as having reached (puberty)»,[[Recorded by Ibn Hibban (4728) and al-Daraqutni (4202), from Ibn ʿUmar; we have not found it with this wording in al-Hakim, and it is agreed upon without mention of puberty.]] and in the other: «He permitted me and saw me as having reached (puberty)».[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2664) and Muslim (1868/91), with the wording: "He permitted me," without mention of puberty.]]

But the word "reached" (balaghtu): does it mean "I reached the age of legal responsibility," or "I reached the state in which I could fight"?

There is a possibility. But ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, may Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him, «wrote to his governors that they should assign stipends to whoever had reached fifteen years, and he saw that they had reached (puberty), and said: if this age is the limit for their fitness for fighting, then it is the limit for their puberty»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2664) and Muslim (1868/91), from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar.]].

Some scholars, such as Abu Hanifa, hold that the limit of puberty is eighteen years, not fifteen years. This is what the regulation of work and workers here follows, because the one who drafted it, apparently, is a foreigner who knows only the well-known school in the street among the common Muslims, which is the school of Abu Hanifa that restricts it to eighteen years. But the schools of the three Imams hold that puberty is attained at fifteen years.

As for the growth of pubic hair, it is the same: there is disagreement. Those who said it is not a sign of puberty said: the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, uncovering the garments of the Banu Qurayza, whoever had grown pubic hair was killed, does not mean that he is legally responsible. Rather, it is evidence that he is among those fit for fighting, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would kill him.

But the well-known position of the school is what is known to you: that puberty is attained by one of three things.

He said: ﴿let them seek permission⁠﴾. He addressed them directly, because when they reach puberty they become fit for legal responsibility, and the address is directed to them.

His saying: ﴿as those before them sought permission⁠﴾, i.e., from the general people who seek permission at all times.

﴿Thus God makes clear to you His signs, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise⁠﴾. ﴿Thus⁠﴾ means: like that clarification, He clarifies. We have said previously that the particle kāf is a noun meaning "like," and it is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of "yubayyin" (clarifies).

Here the noble verse is like the verse before it, except for the difference of His saying ﴿His signs⁠﴾ instead of ﴿the signs⁠﴾. Perhaps this, and God knows best, is from variation in discourse or style, though their meaning is the same.

Then God, may He be exalted, said: (﴿And women past child-bearing⁠﴾: those who have ceased from menstruation and childbearing due to old age ﴿who do not hope for marriage⁠﴾ for that reason, ﴿there is no blame on them if they put aside their outer garments⁠﴾ such as the jilbab, the robe, the veil, and the khimar, ﴿without displaying adornment⁠﴾: showing off, ﴿hidden adornment⁠﴾ such as the necklace, bracelet, and anklet, ﴿and it is better for them to be modest⁠﴾) to the end.

﴿al-Qawāʿid⁠﴾ is the plural of (qāʿida).

His saying: ﴿from among women⁠﴾ is an explanation of al-qawāʿid.

Because the article (al) in al-qawāʿid is a relative pronoun (ism mawṣūl), since when the article enters a derived noun, whether it is a passive or active participle, it is a relative pronoun. So al-qawāʿid means: those who have sat (qaʿadna).

His saying: ﴿from among women⁠﴾ is an explanation of al-qawāʿid. But from what did they sit?

The author says: (from menstruation and childbearing), so the meaning of al-qawāʿid becomes: those who neither bear children nor menstruate, because of their age.

It was also said: al-qawāʿid are those who remain in their houses due to old age, because they do not go out due to infirmity and weakness, so they are "qawāʿid."

It was also said: al-qawāʿid is a name for elderly women in general, just as we say "ʿajūz" (old woman), derived from ʿajz (incapacity). We also say "qāʿida," meaning incapable of standing, going, or coming back.

His saying: ﴿who do not hope for marriage⁠﴾: ﴿who⁠﴾ is an adjective of what?

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 24, verses 54–58 (part 7 of 7):**

* Student: For the women past childbearing.
* Shaykh: "For the women past childbearing," or "for the women"?
* Student: For the women past childbearing.
* Shaykh: It is a qualifier of "the women past childbearing." If you say, "from the women who have no hope of marriage," it would imply that there are women past childbearing who do have hope of marriage, and that is not the case. So His saying ﴿who have no hope of marriage﴾ is a qualifier of "the women past childbearing."
Now His saying ﴿لَا يَرْجُونَ﴾ (lā yarjūna, "do not hope"). How is it ﴿لَا يَرْجُونَ﴾ when they are feminine, and ﴿يَرْجُونَ﴾ is a masculine verb?
* Student: The nūn is the nūn of feminine plural (nūn al-niswa).
* Shaykh: And the wāw?
* Student: The wāw is a pronoun (ism fi'l).
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. The wāw is the wāw of the verb, and the nūn is the nūn of feminine plural.
The meaning of ﴿لَا يَرْجُونَ نِكَاحًا﴾ (lā yarjūna nikāḥan, "who have no hope of marriage") is: they do not aspire to it, because of their old age, since no one desires them to marry them, being elderly women.
﴿فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ يَضَعْنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ﴾ (fa-laysa 'alayhinna junāḥun an yaḍa'na thiyābahunna, "there is no blame upon them if they remove their garments"). Without doubt, what is meant by ﴿يَضَعْنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ﴾ is not all garments, in the sense that they would remain naked. This cannot be claimed. So what is meant by "garments"? It is the outer garments that custom has made people wear, such as (the jilbab — says the author — and the rida' (outer wrap), and the qina' (face veil), and the khimar (headcover)). These are the outer items.
So it is permissible for an elderly woman to wear a simple garment and to uncover her hands, her head, her face, her feet and her lower legs, but on the condition that she does not display adornment; ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجَاتٍ بِزِينَةٍ﴾ (ghayra mutabarrijātin bi-zīnah, "without displaying adornment"). If she intends to keep displaying adornment after old age, when they are no longer hoping for marriage, then it is desirable that they appear as those of advanced age. You find her, for example, wearing a bracelet and an anklet, and sitting and showing off before people.
However, this is on the condition that she is not in this state. If she is in this state, it is not permissible. But if the matter is natural, it is permissible for her to remove her garments.
* Student: Even if she is in front of a non-mahram man?
* Shaykh: Yes. Even if she is in front of a non-mahram man, because she no longer hopes for marriage. If she becomes one who seeks to attract, [the permission would not apply]. Other matters beyond this will come, if God wills, in the mention of the benefits (fawā'id).
* Student: "With adornment," ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجَاتٍ بِزِينَةٍ﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, meaning that displaying (tabarruj) is only with adornment; there is no tabarruj except with adornment. I say: this is a description of the reality.
* Student: ﴿وَالْقَوَاعِدُ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾. Is it permissible for her to be taken along for service or something of this sort?
* Shaykh: Yes, if she is elderly and there is no fear. That is, if a person brought in an elderly woman as a servant in the house, it is permissible for her to uncover; there is no objection.
* Student: And a mahram?
* Shaykh: No. The ḥadīths are general: it is not permissible for a woman to travel except with a mahram.
* Student: Is he not present in the house?
* Shaykh: No, this is not a condition, because if the house has no seclusion (khalwa), there is no contradiction.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, [the condition is her] reaching full maturity, completing fifteen years.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
Its meaning is "possessor of the ruling," and the wisdom, what do you say?
* Student: (...), O Shaykh. The principle is that...
* Shaykh: Hardship.
* Student: Hardship brings ease.
* Shaykh: Yes indeed, in it is that hardship brings ease. Let us look at the author's words, since he has a comment on this verse.
He says: (The verse of seeking permission (istī'dhān) is said to be abrogated (mansūkha, naskh), and it is said: no, but people were lax in abandoning seeking permission.) The two opinions we pointed to. The correct view is that the verse is muḥkam (firm, not abrogated), remaining in effect, and that abandoning seeking permission is either due to negligence or due to the cause requiring permission having ceased. As for saying that legal rulings are abrogated by people's abandonment of acting upon them, this has no basis.
* Student: The Shaykh says: "in abandoning," "people were lax in abandoning"?
* Shaykh: In abandoning seeking permission.
* Student: He did not say: they were lax in doing it.
* Shaykh: No, in abandoning it. People were lax in abandoning it, meaning they abandoned it. You mean that what should be said is "they were lax in doing it." That would be if he said "in abandoning it." It is also acceptable to say: "people were lax." In what were they lax, or what was the cause of their laxity? It is the abandonment, the abandonment of seeking permission. Yes.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, from disobedience or violation. If he is negligent, we restricted it. What did we restrict it to? If he is negligent in raising and disciplining him. But if he is not negligent, then no.
* Student: Even if he is mature?
* Shaykh: Where?
* Student: We mentioned (...).
* Shaykh: No. If he is mature, he has become independent in himself. But if he reaches maturity, he becomes like others: if he is able to change the evil he has committed, it becomes obligatory upon him.
We also discussed yesterday the matter of His saying: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَا عَلَيْهِمْ جُنَاحٌ بَعْدَهُنَّ﴾ (laysa 'alaykum wa-lā 'alayhim junāḥun ba'dahunna, "there is no blame upon you or upon them after these [times]") [An-Nur 58]. We said the verse has a manṭūq (explicit meaning) and a mafhūm (implicit meaning). Its manṭūq presents no difficulty, namely the negation of blame, since blame is negated. But its mafhūm is that there is blame upon them at these three times.
[That is] upon the guardians and upon the young children. This is problematic, because young children are not morally responsible (mukallafīn), so that they would bear blame for their disobedience.
* Student: The manṭūq has multiple individual instances, and it is true in one of the instances.
* Shaykh: In one of the instances, yes. We say: the mafhūm does not have generality, so it is true with the existence of one case of the generality, even a single case.

(﴿فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْهِ مَا حُمِّلَ﴾ من التبليغ، ﴿وَعَلَيْكُمْ مَا حُمِّلْتُمْ﴾ من طاعته، ﴿وَإِنْ تُطِيعُوهُ تَهْتَدُوا وَمَا عَلَى الرَّسُول إلَّا الْبَلَاغ الْمُبِين﴾ أي: التبليغ البين).

Allah Most High says to the Prophet (ﷺ), commanding him to tell the people: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾. It has already been mentioned that obedience (ṭāʿah) means conforming to the command by carrying out what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden; this is obedience.

His words ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ repeat the governing particle (al-ʿāmil, the word that governs the case of what follows), which shows that obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ) is an independent obedience, and that what he brought is like what came from Allah. For this reason the scholars said: what is made obligatory by the Sunnah (the Prophet's teachings and practice) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is like what is made obligatory by the Qur'an, whether a command or a prohibition. This is clear, because He made obedience to the Prophet (ﷺ) an independent obedience when He said: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾.

His words ﴿the Messenger﴾: the definite article (al-) here is for a known reference (al-ʿahd), and it is a mental reference (ʿahd dhihnī), meaning: the Messenger who is known among you, who is Muhammad (ﷺ). This is not like His words: ﴿But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger﴾ [al-Muzzammil 16], because His words ﴿But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger﴾ refer to a reference already mentioned (ʿahd dhikrī), as in ﴿We sent to Pharaoh a messenger. But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger﴾ [al-Muzzammil 15–16]. As for this verse, it is a mental reference: meaning the Messenger who is known to you and whom you recognise.

(﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ عن طاعته، بحذف إحدى التاءين خطاب لهم) ﴿But if they turn away﴾. The author says: the meaning of ﴿tawallaw﴾ is "turn away" (taʿarrod), that is the meaning of turning away: refusal. But in terms of the wording, its original form is tatawallaw, for "tatawallaw" is addressed to the people, meaning: "And if you, O people, turn away, then upon him is only what he has been charged with," and so on. But one of the two tāʾs has been deleted.

The grammarians (naḥwiyyūn) disagreed over which was deleted: is it the tāʾ of the present tense (tāʾ al-muḍāraʿah, the prefixed tāʾ that marks the present-tense verb), or the tāʾ that is part of the verb's root?

Some said it is the tāʾ of the verb itself, because the tāʾ of the present tense was brought in for a purpose, so it should not be deleted. Others said it is the tāʾ of the present tense, because the tāʾ of the verb is original, while the tāʾ of the present tense is an addition, and so it is more fitting to delete it than an original letter.

In any case, the disagreement here is verbal; it has no effect on the meaning. What is intended is: tatawallaw.

A parallel to the deletion of one of the two tāʾs is His words: ﴿Therefore I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾ [al-Layl 14]. ﴿Talaẓẓā﴾ means ﴿tatalaẓẓā﴾, and ﴿talaẓẓā﴾ is not a past-tense verb, for otherwise it would say ﴿talaẓẓat﴾. Rather it is a present-tense verb from which one of the two tāʾs was deleted.

﴿But if they turn away, then upon him is only what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with﴾. ﴿Upon him﴾ means upon the Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿What he has been charged with﴾ means the conveying, the clarifying and the calling (to Islam). He (ﷺ) conveyed the message clearly and also called people, as in: ﴿Say: This is my way; I call to Allah﴾ [Yusuf 108].

So the Prophet (ﷺ) had two duties, and the author mentioned only one of them. What was obligatory upon him was to convey and to call, and he did so (ﷺ): he conveyed to the people and called them to Allah, and he fulfilled what was required of him.

﴿And upon you is what you have been charged with﴾. What is it that we have been charged with? We have been charged with obeying him and following him. On this basis, if he fails in what is upon him, he becomes deserving of the consequences of that; and if you fail in what is obligatory upon you, you become deserving of the requital for that.

The Prophet (ﷺ) delivered the clear message, so he fulfilled what he was charged with. But those who turned away did not fulfil what they were charged with. In this there is evidence that the Messenger (ﷺ) is not obliged to guide them.

This is frequent in the Qur'an: ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 22]; ﴿Would you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ [Yunus 99]; ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and Ours is the reckoning﴾ [al-Raʿd 40]. So he is not obliged to guide them. Rather, Allah forbade him to have constriction, narrowness and grief in his chest: ﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress because of what they plot﴾ [al-Naḥl 127]; and He said: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ 3], meaning: destroying yourself because they do not believe.

Likewise, whoever inherits from the Prophet (ﷺ), namely the scholars, is only obliged to convey and to call. As for guiding creation, that belongs to their Creator, blessed and exalted is He; it is not your responsibility to guide them.

Allah Most High said, encouraging obedience to Him: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾. If you obey the Messenger (ﷺ), you will be guided. In this there is an indication of what was mentioned earlier: that what the Sunnah has brought is an independent ruling which must be obeyed and followed, just as what came in the Qur'an is. For this reason He said: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾. Guidance is what is sought. So when the Prophet (ﷺ) commands something, it is not permissible for us to say: "Is there a basis for this in the Qur'an or not? If it has a basis, we accept it; if it has no basis, we do not accept it." That is forbidden, and it is disbelief in the Qur'an itself, because Allah says: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾, and then He says ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾. This shows that everything he brought is truth and guidance, and that there is nothing in it of falsehood or misguidance.

Then He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾. Is this restriction (ḥaṣr) real or relative? In ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the conveyance﴾, is the restriction real?

* Student: Real.
* Shaykh: Real? How can it be real, when it is obligatory upon him to pray, to pay zakah and to fast?
* Student: It is a relative restriction.
* Shaykh: A relative restriction, is that right?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Real. When it is said "a real restriction," it means that anything other than it is negated. Can we say here that the Messenger (ﷺ) is only obliged to convey to the people, and as for performing acts of obedience himself, nothing of that is obligatory upon him?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It is not possible, since there is no qualifier.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No. This restriction is considered relative; that is, with respect to what is obligatory upon him towards you. If He had said: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾ and ﴿Upon him is what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with﴾, and ﴿And upon the Messenger, with respect to you, is only the clear conveyance﴾, but as for guiding you and compelling you to the truth, that is not his responsibility, as Allah Most High said: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 272]. So this restriction indicates what is obligatory upon him towards his community: he is obliged only to the clear conveyance.

* Student: A real restriction with respect to (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, with respect to what is obligatory upon him, not with respect to everything in general. But a real restriction is one that applies to everything, not (...) other than this. The meaning of his saying "relative" is that it is relative to a certain circumstance. If you say, for example, "There is no generous man except so-and-so," this is a restriction meaning that there is no generous man other than him, even though many generous men exist besides him. But it means "there is no generous man except so-and-so," that is, with respect to his tribe for example, or relative to his town, or something similar.

So the restriction is relative. It is not real in meaning, but it is relative to something. When the restriction means "relative to such-and-such," it is relative. When the restriction applies to all, it is?
* Students: Real.
* Shaykh: Real.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed: real and relative.

He says: ﴿upon the Messenger is only the conveyance﴾. "Conveyance" (balāgh) means conveying (tablīgh). The root meaning of balāgh is reaching an end; it is said "balagha kadhā," meaning "he reached." So the one who conveys brings people to a goal, which is the guidance that Allah, glorified and exalted, wants His servants to attain.

The author's statement "al-mubīn (the clear) in the sense of al-bayyin (the evident)" is open to question. It has already been established that al-mubīn can mean al-bayyin (evident in itself), and it can mean "making clear to others," that is, clarifying for others. This depends on the context. Here, balāgh means "clear," or "making clear what was conveyed," meaning: he made clear and manifest what he called to and conveyed. So here al-mubīn means "one who makes manifest," not "evident" as the author said. Which is more eloquent: al-mubīn in the sense of "one who makes manifest," or al-mubīn in the sense of "evident"?
* Student: In the sense of "one who makes manifest."
* Shaykh: In the sense of "one who makes manifest," because al-mubīn in the sense of "one who makes manifest" is evident in itself and makes others clear, whereas al-bayyin alone is evident in itself; it may or may not make others clear. ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾.

(﴿وَعَدَ اللَّه الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَات لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْأَرْض﴾ بدلًا عن الكفار، ﴿كَمَا اسْتَخْلَفَ﴾ بالبناء للفاعل والمفعول، ﴿الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلهمْ﴾ من بني إسرائيل بدلًا عن الجبابرة، ﴿وَلَيُمَكِّنَن لَهُمْ دِينهمْ الَّذِي ارْتَضَى لَهُمْ﴾ وهو الإسلام؛ بأن يظهره على جميع الأديان ويوسع لهم في البلاد فيملكوها، ﴿وَلَيُبَدِّلَنهُمْ﴾ بالتخفيف والتشديد، ﴿مِنْ بَعْد خَوْفهمْ﴾ من الكفار، ﴿أَمْنًا﴾ وقد أنجز الله ما وعدهم).

﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the land﴾, in place of the disbelievers, ﴿as He made successors those before them﴾ (the verb may be read in the active or passive voice), ﴿from the Children of Israel, in place of the tyrants; and He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾, which is Islam, by making it prevail over all other religions and by widening the lands for them so that they possess them; ﴿and He will surely change [their state] after their fear﴾ of the disbelievers ﴿to security﴾. Allah has fulfilled what He promised them.

﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. Promise (waʿd) means granting a person what pleases him, while threat (waʿīd) means warning him of what he dislikes. There is a difference between promise and threat: promise is for what is hoped for of what is loved, and threat is for what is feared of what is dreaded. The poet said:

*And indeed I, even if I threaten him, I am one who breaks my threat and fulfils my promise.*

﴿Allah has promised﴾: that is, He, glorified and exalted, has committed Himself to them in what they love. ﴿Those among you who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: that is, those who combine faith and righteous deeds. Faith has its place in the heart, and righteous deeds have their place in the limbs. Faith alone is not sufficient, and deeds alone are not sufficient, and no deed is righteous unless it is based on faith. Even if its outward form is that of righteousness, if it is not founded on faith, it is not righteous. The matter revolves around both: faith and righteous deeds, and this promise belongs to both of them.

﴿He will surely make them successors in the land as He made successors those before them﴾. This is a promise. The meaning of ﴿He will surely make them successors﴾ is that He will make them successors to others: they will succeed others in the land. The word ﴿in the land﴾ here refers to the genus, not one specific land, but the land in general: in truth, all the earth, the whole land. This is because the earth is Allah's earth: ﴿Indeed, the earth is Allah's; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the good outcome is for the righteous﴾ [al-Aʿrāf 128].

His words ﴿to whom He wills of His servants﴾ are well known: He gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills. ﴿And We have already written in the Psalms (al-Zabūr, the book given to David) after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ 105]. On this basis, for example, the land of the Arabs does not belong to the Arabs, the land of the Persians does not belong to the Persians, and the land of the Romans does not belong to the Romans. To whom does the land belong?
* Students: To Allah.
* Shaykh: To Allah. He gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills, namely the righteous servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Whoever disbelieves in Allah and rebels against His obedience has no right to the land; the right belongs to someone else. Allah gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills of His righteous servants.

On this basis, if the Children of Israel say: "The land of al-Sham is ours, because Moses, peace be upon him, said: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has prescribed for you﴾ [al-Māʾidah 21]," then Allah has prescribed it for them here. If the Children of Israel say this, we say: Yes, Moses said this, because at that time you were the people of righteousness, and you were the righteous servants of Allah. The land belongs to Allah, who gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants. So it was yours at that time, without doubt. But when Islam came and you disbelieved in it, you were no longer worthy of it, and its people became whom?
* Students: The righteous.
* Shaykh: The righteous: those who believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) and follow him.

So when the Muslims were expelled, before that, it was occupied after the Jews by whom? By the Christians, the Romans, because they were the righteous after the Jews. Then after the Romans it was occupied by whom? It was occupied by the Muslims, because they were the righteous servants of Allah. So the land, the land of al-Sham, had been written for whom? For the righteous: ﴿And We have already written in the Psalms after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾. The Children of Israel inherited it from the tyrants because they were upon the truth, meaning the Jews, I mean. Then the Christians inherited it from the Jews because they were the people of truth. Then the Muslims inherited it from the Christians because they were the people of truth.

On this basis, the Jews now have no right to Palestine or to any other part of Allah's land. They have no right to the land ever, neither they nor any disbeliever, because the land is deserved only by whom? By the righteous servants of Allah.

But if the Muslims become righteous and return to their true religion, through which Allah gives them His land as inheritance, then we affirm with certainty that they will regain the land: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the land as He made successors those before them﴾ [al-Nūr 55]. So we affirm with certainty that if the Muslims now truly return to the religion of Allah, with faith and righteous deeds, they will drive the Jews out of the land. Indeed, they will drive the Americans out of their places, and the Russians out of their places. Do we affirm this with certainty or not?

But as long as they (the Muslims) remain in this condition, according to the legal principles and the texts, they do not deserve victory, because they have not struggled against themselves, let alone struggled against others to bring them into Islam. We say: Now establish Islam among yourselves, establish the religion of Allah among yourselves; then afterward Allah will give victory to His religion if you uphold it. For He does not give victory to a person because he is so-and-so, or to this group because they are Arabs, or to that group because they are (...). He gives victory to whoever upholds this religion. Was Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi of Arab origin or not?
* Students: Not Arab.
* Shaykh: Not Arab. Nevertheless Allah gave him victory over the Christians, because he upheld the religion of Allah. The religion itself is what gives victory. It is (...) of itself (...). It is a weapon even if it is not carried. Do not say: Islam is a weapon by which one can decide victory with whatever weapon is in his hand, never. If there is (...) a weapon in Islam in a person's hand, then for us the material weapon remains; that is, with whatever is most powerful in material terms.

It is well known that the Muslims are, at the present time, the weakest of nations in material terms, because they are scattered and dispersed nations, and the enmities among them are many, and the hatred among them is great. This one calls to such-and-such, and that one calls to such-and-such, and this one has a particular school of thought; they are all divided. Allah Most High has said: ﴿Indeed, those who divide their religion and become sects, you have nothing to do with them﴾ [al-Anʿām 159]. This matter applies completely to the Muslims at the present time. There is no unity upon Islam, and no upright religion established among the Muslims. There may be a small faction in which there is some righteousness, of faith and righteous deeds, but even that is weak.

In summary: this promise which Allah has made is true, but to whom? To those who believe and do righteous deeds. These are the righteous servants of Allah about whom Allah said: ﴿And We have already written in the Psalms after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ 105].

So when those who are now fighting the Jews say: "We will drive out the Jews, and establish on these blessed lands which they have occupied (...) an Islamic state that leads people by the religion of Allah, by the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ)," and they first exemplify that themselves before they conquer these lands, then at that point we will be certain of their victory. Otherwise, victory is not guaranteed; rather it may be the opposite, and defeat is what is guaranteed, because whoever undertakes something and struggles for it while acting contrary to it, that is a kind of deception of Allah, mighty and majestic. And whoever deceives Allah, He deceives him.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 24, verses 54–58 (part 2 of 7):**

﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth﴾. It was said: what is meant by "the earth"?
* Students: The genus (all lands).
* The Shaykh: The genus. That is, it is not a specific land, such as the land of Makkah, where Allah makes the emigrants successors in place of the polytheists. It is all the earth.

﴿as He made successors those before them﴾. His saying, ﴿as He made successors﴾, is in reality like His saying: ﴿"Yes, but that my heart may be at rest"﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:260]. That is, it is mentioned for the sake of emphasis and to reassure the one promised of what he was promised. It is as if He said: look at this promise that Allah made to you; it has been fulfilled among those before you.

﴿as He made successors those before them﴾. Like whom? (...) Like the Children of Israel, who succeeded the tyrants. Correct. And also the Children of Israel who succeeded the Pharaohs, for Allah the Exalted says: ﴿"Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it"﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:59]. He also says: ﴿"And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern parts of the earth and its western parts, which We had blessed"﴾ [al-A'raf 7:137]. And the Exalted said: ﴿"How many they left behind of gardens and springs"﴾, that is, Pharaoh. ﴿"How many they left behind of gardens and springs, and crops and a noble station"﴾ [al-Dukhan 44:25–26]. These gardens, springs, crops and noble station of this world, they left to whom? To the Children of Israel. Allah caused them to inherit.

Likewise the Muslims. Allah the Exalted said concerning the Jews, who were subjected to judgment through the killing of the Banu Qurayzah, and then (...) the conquest of Khaybar: ﴿"And He caused you to inherit their land and their homes and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden"﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:27]. That is, you had never stepped upon it, never; Allah caused you to inherit it. And this is a true promise.

You know from history that when the Muslims truly represented Islam, they possessed the eastern and western parts of the earth, and nations submitted to them completely. In reality, they conquered those lands first of all through religion and morals. Whoever examined the conditions of the Muslims found that people entered Islam without any fighting. Yet, despite that, they resorted to weapons so that no one would stand in the way of their call. So the use of weapons in Islam is in reality only a defense of Islam, not a compelling of people to enter by the sword, because Allah says: ﴿"There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become clear from the wrong"﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:256]. And He says: ﴿"And fight them until there is no fitnah"﴾ [al-Anfal 8:39], that is, obstruction from the path of Allah and standing against the Islamic call. ﴿"And religion will be entirely for Allah"﴾. So the religion of Allah is apparent and it is dominant.

In any case, we say: whoever examines the history of the nations before this one and of this one, will know the fulfillment of this promise, and that it is a promise that is fulfilled (...), and that it is only unfulfilled because of deficiency; either in faith (...).

Why, then, was victory withheld at Uhud?
* Students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, because they abandoned righteous deeds, which is obedience. The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Do not leave your place, whether we are victorious over them or they are victorious over us."[[Reported by al-Bukhari (3039) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib.]] But they left, and victory was withheld at the battle of Hunayn because of deficiency in faith, which is reliance upon Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Rather, they relied on their strength and their numbers, and said: "We will not be defeated today because of our small number,"[[Reported by Abu Dawud (2611), al-Tirmidhi (1555), and Ibn Majah (2827) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] so they were defeated because of their small number.

This is evidence that whenever one of the two attributes, faith or righteous deeds, is lacking, one is deprived of this promise to the degree that those two attributes are lacking.

He said: ﴿"as He made successors those before them"﴾. The second matter that Allah promised the believers is: ﴿"And He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them"﴾. This is the delight of their eyes, the delight of the eyes of the believers, that Allah establishes for them their religion which He has approved for them, and Islam is the one that is established, the one that is apparent and dominant. This is the delight of the eyes of the believers. And even if it is not like the first, it is more worthy than it for the true believer who desires faith and Islam.

If he were asked: what do you wish for? He would not say: I wish to have a luxurious car and an elevated palace, and things like that. He would say: I wish to find Islam exalted and established upon the earth. That is his wish, and this is a lofty wish for every believer.

In His saying ﴿"their religion"﴾, the attribution to them contains a kind of specification and a kind of pride and admiration: the religion that they chose for themselves and that became specifically theirs.

Then in His saying ﴿"which He has approved for them"﴾, we say there is also another distinction: that this religion they chose is the religion that Allah also approved for them. So this religion has a distinction and a privilege for the believers from two aspects:
First: it is what they took and chose for themselves.
Second: Allah also approved it for them, so that they would submit to Allah through it. So there are two excellences: an excellence from the side of the one who follows it, and an excellence from the side of the Lawgiver. The followers are ﴿"their religion"﴾, and the Lawgiver is ﴿"which He has approved for them"﴾. They are pleased with this religion and their Lord is pleased with it for them. So this religion, which they accepted for themselves and which Allah approved for them, is the most dear thing to them: that Allah establishes this religion for them.

This is the second result of faith and righteous deeds. The first: succession upon the earth. The second: that Allah establishes their religion for them, makes them firm, strengthens them, and makes it superior over others.

The third benefit: ﴿"And He will surely replace them, after their fear, with security"﴾. We say: there are two readings for it: the light form ﴿"yubdilannahum"﴾ with the lightened verb, and the emphatic form ﴿"yubaddilannahum"﴾, and they have the same meaning, or with a slight difference.

﴿"after their fear, with security"﴾. His saying ﴿"after their fear"﴾: the use of ﴿"after"﴾ (min ba'd) rather than saying "their fear replaced by security" establishes the first fear, and then after it comes security and the manifestation of the blessing of security. Its benefit after fear is more eloquent than security upon security, or not? Because one does not know the value of things except through their opposites. So if it is assumed that this person was in fear, and then after fear he was given security, the security becomes manifest to him; that is, its effect on his soul becomes manifest, and it is more eloquent than if it were security upon security.

For this reason, now these young people (...) of ours, who have lived in this abundant shade and ample bounty, with food from hunger and security from fear, do they appreciate the blessing of this security? Never. They do not appreciate it. It seems to them only an ordinary matter that cannot change. Likewise, they do not appreciate the blessing of being satisfied. It seems to them only an ordinary matter upon which they were created, and it does not change. But whoever has tasted the pain of hunger and the terror of fear, from those who came before them, and then reached this bounty, they know the worth of this bounty. They are those who spent nights unable to be satisfied except with tree leaves if available, and who did not eat meat except the roasted tender parts of camels if they were available. Those are the ones who knew the value of this blessing, which has become such that meats are thrown on garbage heaps because there are no eaters for them.

In any case, my point is that security after fear is far more manifest than security upon security. In reality, the continuation of security among a people who have not tasted the terror of fear does not become apparent; they may not even feel it. But the truth of the matter is that the manifestation of the blessing of security only occurs when it comes after fear.

There is no doubt that those who were first addressed by this verse had tasted the terror of fear, or not? Yes, because they were afraid of their enemies, the disbelievers, due to the severe harm they suffered, verbal and physical. Even the Prophet (ﷺ) did not leave Makkah except in fear and concealment (ﷺ), until Allah the Mighty and Majestic made him prevail, and he entered victorious, triumphant, and supported. So if a person imagines the replacement of fear with security, he finds that fear has a great effect on the soul: ﴿"after their fear, with security"﴾.

Then he said: (And Allah has fulfilled His promise), since the Prophet (ﷺ) said, while standing at the door of the Ka'bah on the year of the conquest, proclaiming the tawhid that had been fought against in that very place: "There is no god but Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and defeated the confederates alone."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1797) and Muslim (1344/428) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]] And it has come to pass, and praise be to Allah. The idols were inside the Ka'bah and around the Ka'bah. This completely contradicts the testimony that there is no god but Allah. The Muslims among them were at times unable to circumambulate the House or pray around it, and if one prayed around it, he was mocked and harmed. Even their leader Muhammad (ﷺ) was "prostrating, and around him were Abu Jahl and those with him from the wicked of Quraysh. They said: Will no one volunteer to go and bring the entrails of the camel of the Banu so-and-so and throw it upon Muhammad (ﷺ) while he is prostrating? So the most wretched of the people set off, brought it, and placed it upon the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was prostrating. They began laughing and mocking him, to the point that some of them fell over from laughter and scorn, until his daughter Fatimah came, she being young and they not daring to prevent her, and she removed it from his back (ﷺ)."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (240) and Muslim (1794/107) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]

I say: this House, whose condition for the Muslims was of this description, after a short time, and praise be to Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) stood on the threshold of the door as judge over the Quraysh, who had done to him what they had done. He said to them: "What do you think I will do to you?" They said: "A noble brother and the son of a noble brother." And in this position, in which he could take revenge as he wished (ﷺ), he said to them: "I say to you what Yusuf said: ﴿'No reproach will there be upon you today; may Allah forgive you'﴾, go, for you are the freed ones (al-tulaqa'), go, for you are the freed ones."[[Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar (5331) and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi (18275) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] So what empowerment is stronger than this empowerment, and what honor is higher than this honor?!

Allah the Blessed and Exalted spoke truthfully in His promise within a short period, and praise be to Allah. Otherwise, who would believe that within eight years, and the Prophet (ﷺ) leaving in the condition you know, he would return victorious, triumphant, and supported?

He says: (Allah has fulfilled His promise to them by what was mentioned, and praised them by His saying: ﴿"They worship Me, not associating anything with Me"﴾). The author holds that this sentence is a resumptive sentence (istinafiyyah) for praise of them: ﴿"They worship Me, not associating anything with Me"﴾. But it is possible that this sentence is a resumptive sentence whose purpose is not praise, but rather the continuation of the attribute of faith and righteous deeds. That is, this empowerment, this succession, and this replacement of fear with security: when does it happen? It happens when they continue to worship Allah the Glorified and Exalted without associating anything with Him. So this sentence would be a circumstantial clause (hal) that gives a broader explanation: that this attribute, or this promise that Allah made, is realized when? When they continue in the worship of Allah and do not associate anything with Him.

Take this attribute, namely sincerity of tawhid to Allah and persistence upon it, which is a condition for empowerment, together with His saying the Exalted: ﴿"And Allah will surely support whoever supports Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might. Those who, if We establish them upon the earth, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong"﴾ [al-Hajj 22:40–41]. These four attributes, together with this attribute, which is worship without association, become the causes of the victory that Allah promised. How many? They are five: worship of Allah without association, whose highest form is tawhid, then establishing prayer, giving zakah, enjoining good, and forbidding evil. These are the true causes of victory by which Allah supports His servants. Anything other than that is not one of the causes of victory.

Note that the preparation of strength falls within these matters, does it not? Yes, it falls within these matters, because it is part of worshipping Allah, since Allah commanded it, and everything that Allah commanded is among the acts of worship.

As for a man who says: I wish for victory, but he does not establish prayer, from where will victory come to him?! He wishes for victory, but he does not enjoin good or forbid evil, so from where will victory come to him?! There must be enjoining of good and forbidding of evil. Be certain that the Muslims' affairs will never stand firm except through enjoining good and forbidding evil, because if they do not enjoin good and forbid evil, it necessarily leads to division among them, does it not?

I tell you now: if people do not enjoin good and forbid evil, it definitely and necessarily leads to their dividing, because are the people's drinking-place one and their goal one? No. This is a matter of necessity. So if the one who has deviated from Islam is not corrected, he becomes separated from us, following a path other than ours. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿"And let there be among you a community calling to good, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong. And those are the successful"﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:104], and ﴿"And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them. And for them is a great punishment"﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:105]. So all of this division results from abandoning enjoining good and forbidding evil, and it is a natural, realized matter.

He says: ﴿"They worship Me, not associating anything with Me"﴾. His saying ﴿"not associating anything with Me"﴾: "anything" (shay'an) is an indefinite noun in a negative context, so it encompasses any thing that might be associated with Allah. Shirk is not restricted to worshipping an idol, such as a person bowing and prostrating to a tree, a stone, a grave, the sun, or the moon. No, shirk is more general than all of that. Even when a person obeys others in disobedience to Allah, that is shirk: ﴿"They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah"﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:31]. "'Adi ibn Hatim said: O Messenger of Allah, we do not worship them. He said: 'Do they not make lawful what Allah has made unlawful, and you make it lawful, and make unlawful what Allah has made lawful, and you make it unlawful?' He said: Yes. He said: 'That is their worship.'"[[al-Tirmidhi (3095) and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (218), with its wording, from the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim.]]

A man who prefers this world and puts it ahead of the Hereafter: is he a polytheist or not?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: He is a polytheist, because of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Wretched is the servant of the dinar, wretched is the servant of the dirham."[[Reported by al-Bukhari (2886) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] Because the root of worship (ibadah) is taken from humiliation (dhull). From it comes the expression "a paved road" (tariq mu'abbad), meaning one made smooth (mudhall) for those who travel upon it, who walk over it. So a person being humbled before the dirham and the dinar, to the point of preferring them over obedience to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, is a kind of shirk. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) called him a worshipper of it.

The phrase ﴿"not associating anything with Me"﴾ is not a light expression if we conceive its meaning as it came in the Book and the Sunnah. But if we restrict its meaning and say: ﴿"not associating anything with Me"﴾ means they do not worship a tree or a stone, then it becomes narrow, and it has no sense of generality. Thus, true worship of Allah is only realized by the complete absence of shirk, such that one associates no one with Allah, not only in the act of worship itself but also in worship and intention and other things. If this matter is realized, then sincerity has been realized.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 24, verse 54–58 (part 3 of 7):

I have told you that some of the early scholars (salaf) used to say: "I have never struggled against my soul over anything as I have struggled over sincerity (ikhlas)." This is indeed true. Sincerity (ikhlas) means that a person does not associate anything with Allah, neither in worship that is due to Allah alone, nor in intention. This is something very difficult for a person to achieve, but with the help of Allah, the Exalted, and seeking His aid, the desired goal is attained.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: (﴿They worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾ is a new sentence (mustaʾnaf) in the sense of giving a reason (ta'lil)). The author is strange! He made it a praise of them at first, then made it a reason. In reality, there is no doubt that it is a reason, as we have established, but it includes praise, because they worshipped Allah and did not (...).
* * *
﴿And establish the prayer, and give the zakah, and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy﴾. ﴿Establish the prayer﴾ means: perform it upright (qiyman) in the manner that Allah and His Messenger have prescribed. This is the meaning of establishing the prayer. Establishing a thing means making it correct and upright; its opposite is distorting it through corruption and deficiency. So the meaning of "establish the prayer" is: perform it complete.

The word "prayer" (salah) includes both obligatory and voluntary prayer. Therefore, when a person begins a voluntary prayer, it becomes obligatory for him to perform it as it was legislated. If a person wanted to perform a voluntary prayer, and omitted, for example, the glorification (tasbih), or the takbir, or the tashahhud, and said, for example: "It is a voluntary matter, so it is all one," we would say to him: "It was voluntary before you entered into it; but once you have entered it, performing it in the legislated manner becomes obligatory."

If he said: "I want to pray a voluntary prayer, and I prostrate before bowing (...)," or "I want to pray and prostrate only once, is that not voluntary?" We would say to him: "This is not permissible, because even if it is voluntary, performing it in the legislated manner is obligatory."

As for Allah's words, ﴿and give the zakah﴾, it means: give it to those who deserve it. Allah, the Exalted, has explained who deserves zakah in His words: ﴿Zakah is only for the poor and the needy, and those employed to collect it, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and for freeing captives, and for those in debt, and for the cause of Allah, and for the traveler stranded﴾ [al-Tawbah 60] (...).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: ﴿and give the zakah and obey the Messenger﴾. Obedience (ta'ah) has already been explained: it is conformity to the command, doing what is commanded and abstaining from what is forbidden.

His words ﴿and obey the Messenger﴾ are an instance of conjoining the general to the specific (ʿatf al-ʿam ʿala al-khass), for establishing the prayer and giving zakah are themselves part of obeying the Messenger. But this is to draw attention to the excellence of establishing the prayer and giving zakah.

His words ﴿the Messenger﴾: the definite article (al) is for mental reference (al-ʿahd al-dhihni); that is, the Messenger who is well known to you, and he is Muhammad ﷺ.
﴿that you may receive mercy﴾. The author says: "(i.e., hoping for mercy)." This shows that the author took (la'alla) to express hope (raja'), but with regard to the agent (fa'il), not with regard to the speaker. That is, you do these things so that you may be shown mercy, hoping thereby for mercy. So here (la'alla) expresses hope. But with regard to whom?
* Student: The agent.
* Shaykh: With regard to the agent, who is the addressee, not with regard to the speaker. For the speaker, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, nothing is beyond Him so that He would hope for it. It is also permissible to take (la'alla) to mean causation (ta'lil), and then it is with regard to whom? With regard to the speaker, that is: obey Allah and obey the Messenger, because that is a cause of your being shown mercy. This is closer to the meaning; for (la'alla) in the speech of Allah, and indeed in the speech of every speaker, is understood according to what the speaker intends, not what the addressee intends.

On this basis we say: (la'alla) is for causation.
* This indicates that establishing the prayer, giving zakah, and obeying the Messenger are a cause of Allah's mercy.

His words ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾: from whom is it?
* Students: From Allah.
* Shaykh: From Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* Benefits of this verse: the obligation of establishing the prayer, giving zakah, and obeying the Messenger. From where do we derive the obligation?
* Students: From the command.
* Shaykh: From the command, because the basic principle of a command is obligation.
The excellence of zakah, in that it is joined with prayer. It is mentioned together with prayer in many places in the Qur'an. The reason for this, Allah knows best, is that zakah is a purely financial act of worship, and prayer is a purely physical act of worship, and both are of one kind; therefore Allah urged both of them.
* And in it: what is established in the Sunnah is like what is established in the Qur'an, based on His words: ﴿and obey the Messenger﴾. This includes what the Prophet, peace be upon him, said at the outset, and what he said as an explanation of the Qur'an.
* So in it is evidence for the obligation of acting upon the Sunnah just as acting upon the Qur'an is obligatory.

The evidences for this are very numerous, but it is necessary to focus on them, because at a certain time there appeared among the heretics (zanadiqah) those who say that acting upon what is in the Sunnah is not obligatory (...). They confiscated the books of Sunnah, such as the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim; they confiscated them and withheld them from the markets, because they hold that the Sunnah need not be acted upon. Indeed, according to the implication of this action of theirs, the Sunnah is misguidance; for it is not (...) for the books and withheld from people, unless they were a cause of their corruption and misguidance.
* It is also derived from this verse: the affirmation of causes, and that causes have an effect by their own nature. From where is this taken?
* Students: ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾, since He made these three things, establishing the prayer, giving zakah, and obeying the Messenger, a cause of mercy. And the correct view, as we have indicated earlier, is that the cause has an effect by its own nature, but is it independent of Allah, or by the permission of Allah?
* The students: By the permission of Allah.
* Shaykh: By the permission of Allah. As for one who says that the cause is not effective, and that it is merely a sign and indication, his saying is refuted by reason and reality.
* And in it: the excellence of these three matters, since they are a cause of Allah's mercy, namely establishing the prayer, giving zakah, and obeying the Messenger.
* And in it is evidence that prayer is better than zakah, because it is mentioned before it in every place, except that there may be a specific reason for mentioning spending before prayer; sometimes spending is mentioned before prayer. But whenever prayer and zakah are mentioned, prayer is mentioned first.
* * *
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve will escape [Allah] in the earth﴾.

He says: (﴿Do not think﴾ with the feminine and masculine forms [i.e., tahsabanna and yahsabanna] and the agent is the Messenger ﷺ). As for His words ﴿Do not think﴾, it is an address in the author's understanding to the Messenger. But there is a second possibility: that the address is to whom? To everyone to whom such an address is valid, so that this is more general: ﴿Do not think﴾, O addressee, the Prophet, peace be upon him, and others.

As for the reading with the yā' (yahsabanna): ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think﴾, the author also says that the pronoun refers to the Messenger; that is, let not the Messenger think that those who disbelieve will escape in the earth.

But in my view there is a closer possibility: that we take the agent of yahsabanna to be (those who), ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think they will escape in the earth﴾, and the first object of yahsabanna is omitted, the estimate being: Let not those who disbelieve think themselves to be escapers in the earth. In this there is a threat to them.

As for what the author held, the purpose is not to threaten these disbelievers, but the intent is to strengthen the Messenger, peace be upon him, and reassure him that these disbelievers will never escape Allah, the Exalted, but He gives them respite and may delay their punishment.

His words ﴿escape [Allah]﴾: the author says: (from us). A muʿjiz (one who escapes) is one who does what another cannot do and is unable to do. So are the disbelievers escapers from Allah, that is, doing what Allah is unable to do?

The answer: No. ﴿And Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on earth. Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent﴾ [Fatir 44].
(i.e., that they would elude us): this is an explanation of "escape"; that is, we would be unable to reach them, and they would elude us.
﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve﴾ or ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think﴾: this prohibition, as we said, if the address is to the Prophet, peace be upon him, or to everyone to whom address is valid, is for strengthening, reassurance, consolation, and the like. If the pronoun is ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think﴾, according to what we indicated, that the agent is (those who), what is the purpose of the prohibition?
* Student: The threat.
* Shaykh: The threat.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾ their return; the destination is it). ﴿Their refuge﴾ means their return, to which they retreat; the Fire.

He said ﴿their refuge is the Fire﴾ because this is the reality: this worldly life will come to an end, and the return beyond which there is nothing else is that to which the believer and the disbeliever return on the Day of Resurrection: either to a Fire or to a Garden. These people, their refuge is the Fire, may Allah protect us, their return.

His words ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾: the lam is in response to an oath, introducing the oath; that is, by Allah, wretched is the destination. And "wretched" (bi'sa), as is well known, is a verb of blame, or a verb that is fixed in form for expressing blame; and "the destination" (al-masir) is its agent (fa'il). Where is the specified object (makhsus)? Because (bi'sa) and (ni'ma) require an agent and a specified object (...). What did we say?
* Student: They require an agent and a specified object.
* Shaykh: That is not what we said, and you are not saying it either; for (laysa) is among the fixed-form verbs and does not require (...). What did we say, everyone?
* Students: (ni'ma) and (bi'sa).
* Shaykh: (ni'ma) and (bi'sa) require an agent and a specified object. The agent in this verse, ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, is (the destination). Where is the specified object? It is omitted or implicit; the meaning is "wretched is the destination, it," but one cannot say it is "implicit" in the sense of a hidden noun; rather it is a hidden pronoun, and it is the agent. So the object is omitted: either it is said, "wretched is the destination, the Fire," or "wretched is the destination, it."
* Derived from this verse: the perfection of the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that the disbelievers, however great their power, are not able to escape Allah; and that Allah giving them respite does not indicate His inability over them, but rather indicates His wisdom in delaying the punishment for them. This is one point.
* Second: it is evidence that the people of the Fire abide in it forever, based on His words ﴿and their refuge is the Fire﴾; for if they did not abide forever, their refuge would be what lies beyond the Fire, since "refuge" means the final return. This is evidence that the Fire is perpetual for them and that they abide in it forever.

The eternal abiding of the people of the Fire is affirmed in the Noble Qur'an in three verses (...): ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Nisa' 169], ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Ahzab 65], ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Jinn 23].
* Student: I do not remember them (...).
* Another student: Do you remember the places?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: In surah al-Nisa'.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: And in surah al-Tawbah.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: In surah al-Ahzab.
* Shaykh: In surah al-Ahzab, yes indeed. As for surah al-Nisa', His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and do wrong, Allah will never forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Nisa' 168-169]. That is in surah al-Nisa'. In surah al-Ahzab: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever, they will find no protector or helper﴾ [al-Ahzab 64-65]. In surah al-Jinn: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Jinn 23]. These are three clear verses and an explicit text affirming their eternal abiding.

By this, the weakness of the view of those scholars who say that there is no eternity for the people of the Fire becomes known; he was confused by His words: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills; indeed, your Lord is the Effector of what He intends﴾ [Hud 107], and was not confused by His words about the people of the Garden: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, he was not confused about it, because He said: ﴿a gift uninterrupted﴾ [Hud 108]; and here, regarding the people of the Fire, He said: ﴿indeed, your Lord is the Effector of what He intends﴾.

But this does not mean that ﴿indeed, your Lord is the Effector of what He intends﴾ means that He will lift this punishment from them. Rather, since this is a retribution against them and an act that is not something a person chooses, so that Allah's favor is recalled through its continuation, He said regarding the people of the Garden: ﴿a gift uninterrupted﴾, and said regarding these: ﴿indeed, your Lord is the Effector of what He intends﴾, so nothing prevents Him from doing what He wills.
* Student: ﴿Remaining therein for ages﴾ [al-Naba' 23] — is it not used as evidence against eternity?
* Shaykh: Yes, that is not correct (...); because first: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾ is connected to what follows it; that is, for ages they will not taste [coolness], and for other ages; or it is said: "ages," that is, long periods of time, and this does not contradict eternity (...); because eternity is... [is it] separate from the ages?
* Student: Periods (...).
* Shaykh: No, never; periods are not possible, because what is meant by this; that is, if you say: this man (...) the entire Fire (...) for ages, the whole eternity is long ages.
In any case, this undoubtedly does not contradict eternity; either we say it is connected to what follows it, and this is weak in my view, or it is said: "ages," the fact that they are many long ages does not contradict eternity, because eternity is long ages.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Never, this has no end; but the people of the Garden have no end either.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No, (ahqab) is the plural of (huqb), which is a period of years; therefore He said: ﴿ahqaban﴾, successive ages, without any end. If we say: a huqb is, for example, eighty years, and we say: ahqaban, that is, long periods, each huqb being eighty, without any end (...). If He had said: ahqaban whose number is such-and-such, it would have been permissible; but even the eternal period is, in reality, ahqaban.
In any case, whatever the matter: however we understand the word ahqab as indicating eternity, it does not contradict the explicit statement of eternity; it does not contradict it at all.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No, that is not correct (...).
We have said that ﴿their refuge is the Fire﴾ indicates eternity; for if they were not eternal, their refuge would be another (...).
* And in it also is evidence of the evil and ill-omened nature of the Fire and its destination; for Allah has blamed it by His words: ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾.
Know that what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, blames or praises is a great matter; for the great does not praise except what is truly great; that is, the great does not see a great thing except that it is truly great, but one who is not great may regard what is not great as great. As for the great, he does not hold in high esteem except what deserves esteem, and does not blame except what is truly blameworthy and whose blame is extensive.
* Student: So a person may imagine that this description (...)?
* Shaykh: It is, in any case, great in relation to human morals, but this greatness is a greatness limited to what humans can attain. Perhaps I say: "This man has great character," because I sat with him a short time and found virtuous character in him, and it is not as it actually is; but when a truly great person who knows matters and assesses them says it, we know his greatness.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No, greater; for in the Garden there is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. So what Allah has mentioned of the Garden and the Fire is not something we can imagine; it is greater and greater still, because there is in them something we do not perceive in this world; therefore they are among the matters that none knows but Allah. The realities of what is in the Garden and what is in the Fire are among the matters that none knows but Allah.

Therefore, according to our understanding, when a person is punished in the Fire, what happens? He burns and dies; but in the Fire of the Hereafter, no: he tastes the punishment and suffers. The view of one who says that they, may Allah protect us, do not feel its heat, and say that they become accustomed to it, is undoubtedly false; this is why Allah says: ﴿We will replace their skins with other skins so they may taste the punishment﴾ [al-Nisa' 56], which shows that they feel and suffer.
* Student: Do they burn, O Shaykh?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 24, verse 54–58 (part 4 of 7):

* In this is evidence of the great ugliness and evil of the Fire, from the fact that Allah the Exalted described it with this description: ﴿And how evil is the destination.﴾

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not reached puberty among you ask permission of you three times.﴾ [An-Nur 58] The benefit of introducing the ruling with the vocative (nida') has already been mentioned, which is alerting and explaining its importance.

We said: addressing it to the believers also contains three benefits: incitement and urging. That is, because of your faith this address is directed at you. The second thing: carrying it out is one of the requirements of faith. The third thing: neglecting this matter is a deficiency in faith.

And His saying: ﴿let those whom your right hands possess ask permission of you﴾, the lam? 

* Student: It is the lam of command (lam al-amr).
* Shaykh: The lam is the lam of command.

(﴿Those whom your right hands possess﴾ from the male and female slaves, ﴿and those who have not reached puberty among you﴾ from the free, and who know the matters of women, ﴿three times﴾ at three times.) This means: this is an explanation of "times"; by "times" is meant occasions.

His saying: ﴿those whom your right hands possess﴾ is, as the author said: (from the male and female slaves), because (alladhina) is a relative pronoun that includes males and females.

And His saying: ﴿whom your right hands possess﴾, meaning: whom you own. He expressed by "right hands" the self, because it is generally the instrument of taking and giving.

And His saying: ﴿and those who have not reached puberty among you﴾ means: those who have not reached an age at which they generally experience wet dreams. Or ﴿have not reached puberty﴾ means: the intellect, i.e., they have not reached the point of being among the sensible/rational. In any case, what is meant by them is those below the age of puberty.

The Shaykh: ... upon you at these times, so they should not concern themselves.

However, there is a point to consider in this restriction; because the purpose of this is not their entering upon women, such that we would say: if they know the matters of women. Rather, the purpose of these instructions is out of fear that they might enter upon a person in a state in which he does not wish to be seen. That is, these three times are times of nakedness (awrah); any person who enters upon you, even if he does not know the matters of women, you undoubtedly feel repulsed by him and averse to this entry.

So the correct view is that this restriction the author mentioned is not intended. Rather we say: those who have not reached puberty; because if they have reached puberty, the ruling concerning them will come, Allah willing.

﴿Three times﴾ [An-Nur 58], meaning: at three times. He explained them by His saying: ﴿before the prayer of dawn﴾ [An-Nur 58], because before the dawn prayer a person is not prepared for someone to see him or enter upon him; he may be in sleepwear, which he dislikes anyone seeing him in, and he may be in clothing even more revealing than that, such as his clothing with his family, and the like.

The second: He said: ﴿and when you put off your clothes at midday﴾ [An-Nur 58], meaning: the time of noon, when you put off (...).

* * *

* Student: ﴿So there is no sin upon them in their not wearing their outer garments, without displaying adornment; but to refrain is better for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ [An-Nur 60]

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. It has preceded that Allah, glorified and exalted, commanded obedience to Allah and His Messenger, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakat, and He explained that this is a cause of the mercy of Allah, blessed and exalted.

We now begin the benefits: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who have believed and done righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, as He made successors those before them﴾ [An-Nur 55].

* First: In this verse is encouragement and inducement to faith and righteous deeds.

* Second: In it is a promise to those who have attained these two qualities that Allah the Exalted will make them successors upon the earth, as He made successors those before them; that is, He will make them successors to its people in inheriting it after them.

* And in it also: evidence of the excellence of illustrative reasoning; since Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned examples for His promise of the matters that occurred: ﴿He will surely make them successors upon the earth, as He made successors those before them﴾. Allah the Exalted intended by this example ﴿as He made successors those before them﴾ to reassure those promised by mentioning that the matter occurred among those before them, so this provides added encouragement to them.

* And in His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who have believed and done righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth﴾ is also evidence that the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants. He is the One who makes people successors in it in place of others, and people have no ownership of this earth; sovereignty over the earth belongs to Allah, who gives it to whom He wills.

* And in it also: evidence that faith and righteous deeds are a cause for establishing the religion on the earth, and that disobedience is a cause for the removal of the religion from the earth; by His saying: ﴿and He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾. From this it is understood that if they were to commit sin and not believe and not do righteous deeds, the religion which is theirs, and which Allah has approved for them, would not be established for them.

In it is a severe warning — this second benefit relates to what precedes it — against what? Against disobedience and shortcoming, and that this is a cause for the removal of the religion from them. This is the consistent pattern of Allah's laws, the Exalted, for blessings that are not thanked disappear, and the greatest blessing Allah bestows upon His servants is the blessing of religion; if it is not thanked, it disappears like other blessings.

* And in this: evidence of the perfection of the Islamic religion, since He said: ﴿which He has approved for them﴾; it is the religion He approved for His servants, so it is the most perfect of religions absolutely, and for this reason the messages were concluded with it.

* And in it also: evidence that faith and righteous deeds are a cause for the continuation of security and the removal of fear; the continuation of security if there was prior security, it continues; and the removal of fear if there was fear, it is removed; by His saying: ﴿and He will surely give them security in place of their fear﴾.

* And in it also: evidence that important matters should be emphasized with various kinds of emphasis, since this promise is one of the important matters, because of the benefits and advantages that result from it in this world and the Hereafter. For this reason Allah the Exalted emphasized it with the oath, the lam and the nun: ﴿He will surely make them successors﴾, ﴿and He will surely give them security in place of their fear﴾.

And He also emphasized it with a semantic emphasis, not a verbal particle, which is His saying: ﴿as He made successors those before them﴾; for the purpose of the particle of comparison — as we have previously stated — what is the purpose of it? It is to emphasize this promise by mentioning its evidences. So that is also a semantic emphasis upon verbal emphasis. The first, which was emphasized by the lam, the nun and the oath, these are verbal emphases; but ﴿as He made successors those before them﴾ contains a semantic emphasis, by mentioning what strengthens and steadies the heart.

* And in it also: evidence that faith and righteous deeds are the worship of Allah; by His saying: ﴿They worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾; and accordingly, the realization of monotheism is one of the causes of this promise which Allah has promised.
